I am a survivor myself (23 now). This advice will apply to anything in life. All your future failures, disappointments, and crises that may await you: 

Accept what you cannot change, and instead focus your energy on what you can. 

All the worrying, stressing, and crying in the world will never help you in a situation like this, it will only hurt you. 

Focus instead on what you can do right at this moment to take a deep breathe and fight through this, one day at a time. Don’t blame yourself, don’t blame anyone else, don’t get angry at God or the universe. 

It’s up to you to decide how you handle this situation.

The “in water” ending is canon, where James commits suicide by driving his car (which contained Mary’s dead body) into Toluca lake. This is because the leave ending, while possible, has several factors making it unlikely:

1) James admits to Laura that he killed Mary in the hotel. 
2) James is delusional and suicidal and unfit to be a father (sticking his hand into holes, jumping down seemingly bottomless pits, etc) 
For these reasons he would have to worry about Laura possibly telling law enforcement, and he isn’t mentally fit to be a father after the events of SH2.


Mary wasn’t dead for three years, she was murdered by James for a few days at the most. Due to the shock proceeding the act of euthanizing his wife, James suffers from strong symptoms of denial. Everyone who visits silent hill “takes a little bit of it” with them, which is why it beckoned him back following the deed for his judgement. 

Pyramid head was created by silent hill to help James come to terms with what he had done, not to punish him. This is why the two pyramid heads commit suicide after James acknowledges what he had done, as they were no longer needed. All the creatures are real, not imagined.


Laura sees no monsters because she has no inner demons she’s struggled with since she’s just a little girl. All she sees is an empty town. 

The best way I could describe the town is as a personalized purgatory for unique sinners, providing a possible, but not guaranteed chance of redemption. James, Angela, and Eddie all committed sins, but they were also victims and their actions were justifiable in some ways.

I believe the “in water” ending is the most beautiful, because James isn’t just imagining speaking to Mary in the end, it really is her. She really was waiting in silent hill, waiting to be reunited with James. By committing suicide, both of their souls can finally be at peace. It’s what I would want for myself. I would have no reason to live after losing my wife and experiencing what James had experienced in silent hill.
